title: Musicians in his father's band: Pick, Selby Thomas, Alonso
summary: He names players in his father's band and describes the young trumpeter Alonso and Tom Albert replacing him.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Barbara? Sure. You mean a Mississippi? Yeah. Sure.

Frank Toast, he played with my daddy. And there was a fellow, they called him Pick, he used to play guitar with my daddy. And Selby Thomas, he was a bass player from the day. See, my daddy, my daddy was playing violin and he had this fellow Selby Thomas. And Selby Thomas, he was playing bass. And, oh, they had another other brother, he used to call him William Alonso. He was a trumpet player. But this little brother, he used to get to high all the time and my daddy, he just got disgusted. And that's when he began to get Tom Alvitt over there to play with him. But he was a good little trumpet player, Moiré.
But he didn't go wrong with Tom Alvitt.
No, no he didn't because I mean Tom Alvitt was a great guy.
What did Moiré and Moiré and Alonso play like? Who would he sound like if you'd know Traylor?

Well, he was on pointy style. Yeah, he was on pointy style. Righty? Yeah. What about his finger? Did he have much finger? Yeah, a lot of finger. Just, you know, like some guys would let a little licker get ahead of him and my daddy would go for him, I'd be looking for him and show up. There he was. He wasn't there. But he was a good little trumpet player. When he was there, he was a good little trumpet player. Yeah, yeah. Did you know Willie Davis that played guitar?
I can't praise him. Well, what did Pick play like?
Did he play with his fingers or with a flat pick? No, no, he played with a flat pick.
